newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close lower and seen weakening.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close lower and seen weakening.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled a dull session lower, and adequate supplies are likely to stymie any attempt from the market to rally, market sources said.
They pegged support at 100.00 and resistance at 105.00, basis the most-active January contract.
"Supplies are more than adequate," said Kevin Marshburn, an analyst with Fimat Futures.
Friday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture put the 1996/97 Florida crop at 220 million 90-lb boxes, towards the high end of market expectations.

Marshburn said that while weekly movement has averaged only around 5 million gallons, it is likely to pick up eventually in light of current pricing levels. The market awaits the weekly data following today's close.
The spot-November contract ended up 0.35 to 112.15. Most-active January settled down 1.60 at 102.35, having ranged from 103.50 to 102.20.
The deferred March and May contracts hit contract lows during the session.
Players dismissed Hurricane Lili, which neared Cuba Thursday.
